did_you_know.text: The biblical Hebrew verb וְיִשְׁאֲלוּ can mean either “ask for” or “borrow.” That is why translations differ slightly in describing the request for silver and gold objects.
The phrase “כַּחֲצֹת הַלַּיְלָה” means “around midnight,” not necessarily at one precisely measured moment. The word “כַּחֲצֹת” indicates an approximate time.
The phrase “not a dog will sharpen its tongue” is a vivid way of saying that no dog will bark. In biblical Hebrew, “sharpening the tongue” can describe a dog’s bark.
